report.tagline: Nintendo's second hybrid console that you can play on the TV or carry as a handheld, and the fastest-selling console launch ever.
report.simpleSummary: The Switch 2 is a games console you can plug into your TV or hold in your hands like a big phone with controllers on the sides. It launched in June 2025 and plays both new games and almost all old Switch games. Nintendo makes most of its money selling its own games, like Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza, to people who own the console. The console is the doorway; the games are the business.

overview.whatItDoes: Switch 2 is a hybrid console: a handheld with a 7.9-inch screen and detachable Joy-Con 2 controllers that also docks to a TV at up to 4K. It plays new Switch 2 games and most original Switch games. Nintendo sells the hardware at a thin margin and makes its profit on its own games and the Nintendo Switch Online subscription.
howItWorks: You buy the console for $449.99 (US launch price) or a bundle with a game.
You play it on the go or drop it into the dock to play on a TV.
Games come on cartridges, as Game-Key Cards (a card that unlocks a download), or digitally from the Nintendo eShop.
Joy-Con 2 controllers attach with magnets and can work like a computer mouse.
GameChat lets friends talk and share screens; a camera accessory shows faces.
Nintendo Switch Online ($19.99 a year, more for the Expansion Pack) adds online play, classic games and cloud saves.
overview.valueProposition: One console for the TV and the commute, with Nintendo games you cannot get anywhere else, and your old Switch library comes with you.

painPoints.pain: You have to choose between a TV console and a handheld.
painPoints.howSolved: Hybrid design: one device does both, and switching takes a second.

painPoints.pain: Upgrading usually means losing your old game library.
painPoints.howSolved: Plays most original Switch games, many with free or paid upgrades.

painPoints.pain: Families want games everyone can play together on one device.
painPoints.howSolved: Two Joy-Con 2 controllers in the box and many local multiplayer games.

painPoints.pain: The original Switch felt slow and low-resolution by 2024.
painPoints.howSolved: Much faster chip, 1080p 120Hz screen and 4K on TV.

painPoints.pain: Playing with distant friends was awkward on Switch 1.
painPoints.howSolved: GameChat with voice, video and screen share built in.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Same console works as a handheld or docked to a TV.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: This is Nintendo's unique position; Sony and Microsoft do not sell a single device that does both.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Runs most of the 157 million-console Switch 1 game library.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lowers the cost of upgrading and keeps old buyers inside Nintendo.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, Pokemon and others only on Nintendo.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Exclusive games are why people buy the console and where most of Nintendo's profit comes from.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Magnetic controllers that can slide on a table like a mouse.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A new way to play that gives developers something PS5 cannot offer.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Voice and video chat with screen sharing, through the C button.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes playing with friends easier, which keeps people coming back and sells more multiplayer games.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid online play, classic NES to GameCube games and cloud saves.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Recurring revenue from the installed base between game launches.

steps.detail: Watches a Nintendo Direct or sees the launch news.
Compares the price with the Mario Kart World bundle.
Preorders at a retailer or the My Nintendo Store.
Moves save data and digital games from the old Switch.
Starts Mario Kart World and some upgraded old games.
Picks up Donkey Kong Bananza and a Switch 2 Edition upgrade.
Kids ask for a Switch 2 for the holidays.
Parent checks price, parental controls and which games are kid-safe.
Picks a bundle at a store with a game included.
Creates child accounts and sets screen-time limits in the Parental Controls app.
Plays Mario Kart together on the TV.
Adds a Nintendo Switch Online family plan for online play.
Sees a new release in the eShop or a friend talks about it.
Compares physical cartridge, Game-Key Card and digital price.
Buys digitally to avoid carrying cartridges.
Waits for the download, sometimes buying a microSD Express card for space.
Plays in short sessions on the commute.

businessModel.summary: Nintendo makes money from three things: selling consoles, selling games (its own and a cut of others'), and Nintendo Switch Online subscriptions. Its own games carry the most profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Console sales at $449.99 and up, plus controllers and accessories. Thin margin, especially early in the life cycle.
Nintendo's own games, often $69.99 to $79.99. Nintendo keeps nearly all the money, minus making and selling costs.
A share, usually around 30%, of every game other publishers sell on the eShop or on cartridges.
From $19.99 a year in the US, with a pricier Expansion Pack and family plans.
The Super Mario Bros. Movie, Super Nintendo World and licensing make the characters more valuable.

businessModel.pricing: US launch: console $449.99, bundle with Mario Kart World $499.99, top first-party games $69.99 to $79.99, Nintendo Switch Online from $19.99 a year. Prices vary by country and Nintendo announced rises in 2026.
costDrivers: Chips, memory and screens for the console, made more expensive by the 2026 memory chip shortage
US tariffs on consoles made in Asia
Game development studios and long development cycles
Marketing, especially at launch and the holidays
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate: on a $449.99 console, after the retailer takes its cut and Nintendo pays for parts, factory, shipping and tariffs, Nintendo may keep only about $20 to $50, or even break even early on. The money comes from what the owner buys next. If an owner buys 3 Nintendo games at $70 in the first year, Nintendo keeps maybe $45 to $55 per game after cartridge and store costs, so about $150. Add a cut of 1 or 2 third-party games (about $20 each) and a $19.99 online subscription, and one owner can bring in about $200 of profit in year one. That is why the attach rate, the number of games sold per console, matters so much.

howTheyGetUsers: Upgrading the 157 million original Switch owners
Nintendo Direct video showcases that announce new games
Big launch games like Mario Kart World bundled with the console
Films, theme parks and merchandise that keep Mario and Pokemon famous
whatBringsUsersBack: A steady release calendar of first-party games
Online play with friends through GameChat and Switch Online
Free updates and paid expansions for big games
Classic games added to the Switch Online library
growth.moat: Nobody else owns Mario, Zelda and Pokemon, and those games only run on Nintendo hardware. Nintendo also has 40 years of trust with parents. The hybrid design has been copied by PC handhelds like the Steam Deck, but those do not have Nintendo's games, so the real moat is the characters and the studios behind them.

competitors.name: Sony PlayStation 5
competitors.positioning: The most powerful mainstream console, aimed at core gamers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Switch 2 is portable, family-focused and built around Nintendo exclusives, not raw graphics.

competitors.name: Valve Steam Deck and PC handhelds
competitors.positioning: Portable PCs that play your Steam library.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Switch 2 is simpler and has Nintendo games; the Steam Deck has cheaper games and a bigger library.

competitors.name: Microsoft Xbox
competitors.positioning: Moving toward Game Pass on many devices, including PC handhelds.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Nintendo still sells full-price games and owns its hardware, while Xbox chases subscriptions.

competitors.name: Mobile games (Roblox, Fortnite, gacha games)
competitors.positioning: Free games on phones every kid already owns.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Switch 2 asks for $449 upfront and $70 games but offers premium, ad-free play.

northStar.metric: Monthly active Switch 2 players and the hours they spend in games
northStar.why: Nintendo's profit comes from games bought over many years. Players who keep playing every month buy more games and renew Switch Online, so active play is the best sign the console is delivering fun.

guardrailMetrics: Customer complaints about prices and Game-Key Cards
Joy-Con 2 and console defect and return rates
Parent trust signals, such as parental control usage and ratings
strengths: Fastest-selling console ever, almost 20 million in its first fiscal year
Exclusive, much-loved characters and in-house studios
Huge upgrade pool of 157 million Switch 1 owners
Backward compatibility protects players' past purchases
Brand trusted by families across ages
weaknesses: Higher prices than the original Switch, for both console and games
Hardware margins are thin and exposed to chip prices and tariffs
Weaker hardware than PS5 means some big third-party games look worse or skip it
Online service and features lag behind Sony and Microsoft
Sales fell about 41% year on year in July to September 2026 as launch demand cooled
risks: Memory chip shortage raising costs and forcing price rises
US tariffs on consoles from Asia
Kids moving to free mobile games like Roblox and Fortnite
Players resisting $80 games and buying fewer titles
Weaker yen or economy cutting spending on games
userComplaints: Games priced at $79.99 feel too expensive
Game-Key Cards are not really physical games; they need a download and do not work offline

pmLessons: The hardware is often not the profit maker. The console wins customers, and the games make the money.
Backward compatibility lowers the cost of switching up, which is why Switch 2 sold so fast.
Keep a strong, unique position. Nintendo does not try to beat Sony on power; it wins on fun, portability and its characters.
Price changes hurt trust. Raising prices and adding Game-Key Cards created anger even during record sales.

interviewQuestions.question: Switch 2 sales dropped 41% year on year last quarter. How would you diagnose it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Check if it is normal launch decline, supply, price rise, or a weak game calendar. Split by region and channel. Look at active users and attach rate, not just units.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Nintendo launch a cheaper Switch 2 Lite?
interviewQuestions.hint: Who would buy it (kids, emerging markets), cannibalisation of the main model, chip costs, and effect on installed base and attach rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Switch 2?
interviewQuestions.hint: Monthly active players and play time. Break into installed base, active rate, attach rate and subscriptions.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve Nintendo Switch Online?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a persona, list pains (basic features, value for money), suggest 2 to 3 features, and pick a metric like renewal rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Nintendo sell its games on PC or phones?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare extra game revenue against weaker reasons to buy the console. Consider brand, margins and the role of exclusivity in the moat.
